textbookText: B. Biotic component: Biotic components of pond ecosystem are living beings of pond and are categorized into following groups:

1. Producers: The main producers in pond ecosystem are algae and other aquatic plants. The green plants can prepare their own food by the process of photosynthesis. In pond ecosystem, the producers are phytoplanktons which are minute microscopic floating or suspended plants like Volvox, Spirogyra, Anabaena, Ulothrix, etc. and larger plants known as macrophytes which may be floating, suspended or submerged like Chara, Hydrilla, Marsilea, Eichornia, Lemna etc.

2. Consumers: The consumers in pond ecosystem are categorized as primary, secondary and tertiary consumers. The primary consumers like tadpole, small fishes, etc. consume green plants and algae as their food. They are herbivorous of pond ecosystem. Secondary consumers like frog, big fishes, crabs etc. consume primary consumers as their food. These secondary consumers are consumed by tertiary consumers. The tertiary consumers are water birds, snake, crocodile etc.

3. Decomposers: When aquatic plants and animals die, a large number of bacteria and fungi attack their dead bodies and convert the complex organic substances into simpler inorganic compounds and elements. These micro-organisms are called decomposers.

Functional components The functional aspect of pond ecosystem includes: 1. Flow of Energy 2. Flow of nutrients Figure: 4.1.1 Functional aspect of Pond ecosystem The aquatic green plants of the pond ecosystem capture the solar energy and convert it into chemical energy of food and store in their body through photosynthesis. This process is called primary productivity. The primary consumers like tadpole, small fishes etc. of the pond ecosystem derive the energy by consuming plants or plants parts. These primary consumers are eaten by secondary consumers (like frog, crabs etc.) and then secondary consumers by tertiary consumers (like water birds, snake, etc.). In this chain of eating and being eaten, the aquatic green plants form first trophic level, primary consumers form second trophic level, secondary consumers form third trophic level and tertiary consumers form fourth trophic level. This linear arrangement of trophic levels is called food chain along which the energy flows. At each trophic level some energy is lost as heat and respiration so available energy decreases as one moves away from the first trophic level. The flow of energy is unidirectional. Also, organisms at each trophic level die and generate waste organic material. This constitutes detritus food chain. An ecosystem contains several food chains of each of the above types which are inter-linked forming a food web.

The nutrients in atmosphere, soil, water are utilized by aquatic green plants during photosynthesis, move from organism to organism through food chain and ultimately from all trophic levels, the decomposers break down the complex organic compounds and release nutrients back to atmosphere, water and soil again in a cyclic manner. This is known as biogeochemical cycling. STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL ASPECT OF FOREST ECOSYSTEM Forest ecosystem is the terrestrial ecosystem. Like other ecosystems, forest ecosystem also has two main components: A. Abiotic component B. Biotic component A. Abiotic component: Abiotic components are the non-living things of forest ecosystem. The abiotic components of forest ecosystem are soil, moisture, air, sunlight, etc. B. Biotic component: Biotic components are the living things of forest ecosystem. All the biotic components are grouped into following groups: 1. Producers: All the green plants of a forest are producers. They are the main sources of food for all the animals in forest ecosystem. The producers in the forest ecosystem are trees, shrubs, herbs, lichens, mosses and algae. 2. Consumers: They include all kinds of animals that cannot prepare their own food. On the basis of feeding habit, the consumers are divided into three types i.e. primary consumers, secondary consumers and tertiary consumers. Primary consumers take their food directly from producers. They may be grasshopper, rabbit, deer, monkey, birds and all herbivorous animals. Secondary consumers are wolve, jackal, frog etc which consume primary consumers. The animals like lion, tiger, hawks, etc are called as tertiary consumers as they obtain their food from secondary consumers. 3. Decomposer: They are micro-organisms like bacteria and fungi which attack dead bodies of producers and consumers. It converts complex organic compounds into simpler inorganic compounds and elements which are again utilized by producers in their nutrition.
